The stretch of stream an FDIS site visit fished

Source: R/fdis_span.R
knw_fdis_span.Rd

An FDIS visit is placed on the Freshwater Atlas by one point, its reported UTM snapped to a stream (0230), and records a fished length. Field crews usually report a site's downstream end, so the fished stretch is taken to run upstream from that point for the fished length, along the same blue line, and is cut at the line's top (#23). This is the stretch a fish caught on the visit came from, which is what #137 weighs one discharge value per segment against.

Usage

knw_fdis_span(downstream_route_measure, fished_length_m, line_top_m)

Arguments

downstream_route_measure

numeric, the visit's measure on its blue line, in metres.

fished_length_m

numeric, the fished length, in metres.

line_top_m

numeric, the blue line's top measure (its largest upstream_route_measure).

Value

A data.frame with one row per visit: upstream_route_measure, and flag_span_capped, TRUE where the line's top cut the span short.

Details

A fished length that is missing, zero or a sentinel (9999 or more) gives no span, nor does a point with no measure or one beyond its line's top.

Examples

# a 200 m site 100 m up its stream, and a 300 m one whose stream ends 100 m above its point
knw_fdis_span(c(100, 900), c(200, 300), line_top_m = c(5000, 1000))
#>   upstream_route_measure flag_span_capped
#> 1                    300            FALSE
#> 2                   1000             TRUE
